params.body:
The Werking screen reported every morning that 2.583 photos had been "in processing for more than an hour". It was wrong, and underneath it sat a real hole.

## Why a path breaks

`ImageController::upload_dropzone` writes the photo row with the **temporary** path, `vehicles/<id>/drop/car_image_N.ext`, and `processing = 1`, because the tile has to show something while the job runs. `ProcessVehiclePhoto` then puts the three sizes in the bucket (lines 83, 95, 103), deletes the temporary file, and **only then** updates the row (109 to 115).

Die between the storing and the saving and you get exactly what we found: the file sits on its final path while the row still points at a temporary file that no longer exists.

R S1-6.36 closed the neighbouring case on 18 September: a job that really fails takes its own row back. It does not cover this one. `failed()` runs only when the queue marks the job as failed, and a worker cut off by a deploy or a timeout reports no failure at all. The job is simply gone, the row stays, and the photo is invisible while it exists.

## What it costs, and what it does not

A row without a file renders **nothing**: no broken image, no empty slot. Shane checked that against a Peugeot 5008 at Garage Kenens and the page looked perfect: twelve thumbnails, and exactly twelve platform copies with a file behind them. So nobody sees a gap.

What happens instead is quieter: that dealer uploaded 34 own photos and thirteen reach the window, and no screen tells him.

Counted on 23 September 2026 over the live unsold vehicles: **284 rows** with the flag on 51 vehicles, of which **126 had their file on the final path**. 112 of those 126 sit on one vehicle, a Chevrolet at LEGENDS by Legal Brokers. The other 158 are nowhere, not even on the temporary disk. Youngest case: 14 September, so nothing new is arriving.

## The command

`stocklist:fotos-herstellen` looks for the file where the job would have put it and repairs the path only when it is really there. Without `--apply` it changes nothing and only prints what it would do.

It deliberately does **not** set `media_version` or `media_set`. Those say the derived sizes are ready, which is not true here; without them `VehicleImageService::urlVoor()` falls back to the original, which is exactly right. `stocklist:fotos-afgeleid` can make the sizes later.

A command rather than a one-off script, because the window only closes when storing and saving become one, and until then an interrupted worker can open it again.

Verified locally: 23 tests, 84 assertions across the new test and the rule-catalogue tests; `phpstan analyse` green on the whole project.
params.title: A photo whose file is in the bucket gets its path back
